ontologies.label: exercise
ontologies.definition: Physical activity which is usually regular and done with the intention of improving or maintaining physical fitness or health.

ontologies.label: high-intensity interval training
ontologies.definition: A cardiovascular exercise strategy with alternating short periods of intense anaerobic exercise with less-intense recovery periods.

ontologies.label: ventricular ejection fraction
ontologies.definition: The percentage of the end-diastolic volume pumped out of the heart during SYSTOLE.

ontologies.label: aerobic exercise
ontologies.definition: Sustained exercise that places an increased oxygen demand on the cardiovascular system and promotes an increased efficiency of the body's use of oxygen.

ontologies.label: left ventricular ejection fraction
ontologies.definition: The fraction of the left ventricular end diastolic volume ejected with each beat. The left ventricular ejection fraction is equal to the left ventricular stroke volume divided by the left ventricular end diastolic volume.

ontologies.label: health status
ontologies.definition: The level of health of the individual, group, or population as subjectively assessed by the individual or by more objective measures.

ontologies.label: body composition
ontologies.definition: The relative amounts of various components in the body, such as percentage of body fat.

ontologies.label: body fat percentage
ontologies.definition: The amount of an individual's total body mass that is fat, expressed as a percent.

ontologies.label: body protein percentage
ontologies.definition: The amount of an individual's total body mass that is protein, expressed as a percent.

ontologies.label: body mineral percentage
ontologies.definition: The amount of an individual's total body mass that is mineral, expressed as a percent.

ontologies.label: body water percentage
ontologies.definition: The amount of an individual's total body mass that is water, expressed as a percent.

ontologies.label: exercise equipment
ontologies.definition: equipment used in exercise

ontologies.label: exercise prescription
ontologies.definition: Exercise prescription commonly refers to the specific plan of fitness-related activities that are designed for a specified purpose, which is often developed by a fitness or rehabilitation specialist for the client or patient.

ontologies.label: characteristic of exercise
ontologies.definition: Concept used to describe exercise

ontologies.label: isokinetic exercise
ontologies.definition: An exercise that involves movement at a constant rate with a variable force throughout a specified range of motion.

ontologies.label: isometric exercise
ontologies.definition: An exercise that is performed by exerting force against an immovable object or by holding an object in a static position.

ontologies.label: isotonic exercise
ontologies.definition: An exercise that involves the movement of a constant weight or load through a specified range of motion.

ontologies.label: light exercise
ontologies.definition: 20-60 minutes of exercise which elevates your heart rate to 35-60% of your maximum heart rate performed at least 3-4 times per week." [NCI: C39771] {comment="< 3.0 MET"}

ontologies.label: very light exercise
ontologies.definition: Light exercise for less than 20 minutes, 20-60 minutes of exercise which elevates your heart rate to less than 35% of your maximum heart rate, or light exercise less than 3 times per week.

ontologies.label: moderate exercise
ontologies.definition: 20-60 minutes of exercise which elevates your heart rate to 60-80% of your maximum heart rate performed at least 3-4 times per week." [NCI: C39772] {comment="3 - 6 MET"}

ontologies.label: strenuous exercise
ontologies.definition: 20-60 minutes of exercise which elevates your heart rate to 80-90% of your maximum heart rate performed at least 3-4 times per week." [NCI: C39773] {comment="≥ 6.0 MET"}

ontologies.label: gender
ontologies.definition: Characteristics of people that are socially constructed, including norms, behaviors, and roles based on sex. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time." [NCI: C17357] {comment="Do not use this term for non-human animals."}

ontologies.label: sex
ontologies.definition: The assemblage of physical properties or qualities by which male is distinguished from female; the physical difference between male and female; the distinguishing peculiarity of male or female.

ontologies.label: male phenotype
ontologies.definition: An animal who is observed by researcher or clinician to be male, the sex that ordinarily produces sperm.

ontologies.label: female phenotype
ontologies.definition: An animal who is observed by researcher or clinician to be female, the sex that ordinarily produces ova.

ontologies.label: male gender
ontologies.definition: An individual who reports belonging to the cultural gender role distinction of male." [NCI: C46109] {comment="Do not use this term for non-human animals."}

ontologies.label: female gender
ontologies.definition: An individual who reports belonging to the cultural gender role distinction of female." [NCI: C46110] {comment="Do not use this term for non-human animals."}

ontologies.label: family history
ontologies.definition: A record of a patient's background regarding health and disease events of blood relatives. A patient's family medical history may be important in diagnosing existing conditions.

ontologies.label: medical history
ontologies.definition: A record of a patient's background regarding health and the occurrence of disease events of the individual. In addition, personal medical history may be a variable in epidemiologic studies.

ontologies.label: race
ontologies.definition: A geographic ancestral origin category that is assigned to a population group based mainly on physical characteristics that are thought to be distinct and inherent.

ontologies.label: body weight
ontologies.definition: The mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual. It is expressed by units of pounds or kilograms.

ontologies.label: skeletal muscle mass
ontologies.definition: Total mass of skeletal muscle.

ontologies.label: skeletal muscle
ontologies.definition: A subtype of striated muscle, attached by TENDONS to the SKELETON. Skeletal muscles are innervated and their movement can be consciously controlled. They are also called voluntary muscles.

ontologies.label: body fat mass
ontologies.definition: The mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual‘s fat

ontologies.label: body mass index
ontologies.definition: An individual's weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters." [NCI: C16358] {comment="BMI = body mass / height ²"}

ontologies.label: waist–hip ratio
ontologies.definition: The ratio of the abdominal circumference at the navel to maximum hip and buttocks circumference; looks at the proportion of fat stored on the body around the waist and hip. Carrying extra weight around the waist is a greater health risk than carrying extra weight around the hips or thighs.

ontologies.label: basal metabolic rate
ontologies.definition: The measurement of a subject's energy expenditure when at rest.

ontologies.label: oxygen uptake
ontologies.definition: Oxygen uptake is a measure of a person’s ability to take in oxygen via the respiratory system and deliver it to the working tissues via the cardiovascular system, and the ability of working tissues (predominantly skeletal muscle) to use oxygen.

ontologies.label: right ventricular ejection fraction
ontologies.definition: Right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF), is a measure of the efficiency of pumping into the pulmonary circulation.

ontologies.label: maximum oxygen uptake
ontologies.definition: The highest rate of oxygen consumption a subject reaches during an aerobic capacity test.

ontologies.label: cardiac function
ontologies.definition: Functions of pumping the blood in adequate or required amounts and pressure throughout the body." [] {comment="ICF: b410"}

ontologies.label: cardiac output
ontologies.definition: The total volume of blood pumped by the heart over a set period of time, conventionally one minute; it is calculated as heart rate times stroke volume (CO= HR x SV), and is additionally dependent on preload and afterload for functional output.

ontologies.label: cardiac index
ontologies.definition: The measure of an individual's cardiac output as divided by their body surface area (CI= CO/BSA). This calculation is a useful function to determine an individual's cardiac performance in relation to their body size, providing an overview of global cardiovascular function.

ontologies.label: stroke volume
ontologies.definition: The amount of BLOOD pumped out of the HEART per beat, not to be confused with cardiac output (volume/time). It is calculated as the difference between the end-diastolic volume and the end-systolic volume.

ontologies.label: peak filling rate
ontologies.definition: Peak filling rate (PFR) defined as the maximum dV/dt divided by LV end-diastolic volume was obtained as the index of LV diastolic function.

ontologies.label: time to peak filling rate
ontologies.definition: The interval, in milliseconds, between the point of minimal ventricular volume and the point at which the peak filling rate occurs is labeled as the time to peak filling rate.

ontologies.label: vital capacity
ontologies.definition: The volume of air that is exhaled by a maximal expiration following a maximal inspiration." [MSH: D014797] {comment="VC = TLC -RV"}

ontologies.label: total lung capacity
ontologies.definition: The volume of air contained in the lungs at the end of a maximal inspiration." [MSH: D014109] {comment="It is the equivalent to each of the following sums: VITAL CAPACITY plus RESIDUAL VOLUME; INSPIRATORY CAPACITY plus FUNCTIONAL RESIDUAL CAPACITY; TIDAL VOLUME plus INSPIRATORY RESERVE VOLUME plus functional residual capacity; or tidal volume plus inspiratory reserve volume plus EXPIRATORY RESERVE VOLUME plus residual volume.", comment="TLC = VC +RV"}

ontologies.label: residual volume
ontologies.definition: The volume of air remaining in the lungs after a maximal exhalation." [NCI: C89836] {comment="RV = TLC - VC"}

ontologies.label: maximum voluntary ventilation
ontologies.definition: Measure of the maximum amount of air that can be breathed in and blown out over a sustained interval such as 15 or 20 seconds.

ontologies.label: forced expiratory volume
ontologies.definition: Volume of air that a subject with fully inflated lungs can breathe out per unit time.

ontologies.label: forced expiratory volume in 1 second
ontologies.definition: The volume exhaled during the first second of a forced expiratory maneuver that is started from the level of total lung capacity.

ontologies.label: forced expiratory volume in 3 seconds
ontologies.definition: The volume exhaled during the first three seconds of a forced expiratory maneuver that is started from the level of total lung capacity.

ontologies.label: minute ventilation
ontologies.definition: The volume of gas inhaled (inhaled minute volume) or exhaled (exhaled minute volume) from a person's lungs per minute.

ontologies.label: forced vital capacity
ontologies.definition: The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled following maximal inhalation.

ontologies.label: alveolar ventilation
ontologies.definition: Alveolar ventilation is the exchange of gas between the alveoli and the external environment. It is the process by which oxygen is brought into the lungs from the atmosphere and by which the carbon dioxide carried into the lungs in the mixed venous blood is expelled from the body.

ontologies.label: closing volume
ontologies.definition: The lung volume at which the dependent lung zones cease to ventilate presumably as a result of airway closure.

ontologies.label: tidal volume
ontologies.definition: The volume of air inspired or expired during each normal, quiet respiratory cycle.

ontologies.label: functional residual capacity
ontologies.definition: The volume of air remaining in the LUNGS at the end of a normal, quiet expiration." [MSH: D005652] {comment="It is the sum of the RESIDUAL VOLUME and the EXPIRATORY RESERVE VOLUME."}

ontologies.label: forced expiratory flow
ontologies.definition: The flow (or speed) of air coming out of the lung during the middle portion of a forced expiration.

ontologies.label: blood pressure
ontologies.definition: The pressure of the circulating blood against the walls of the blood vessels.

ontologies.label: diastolic blood pressure
ontologies.definition: The minimum blood pressure in the systemic arterial circulation during the cardiac cycle.

ontologies.label: body temperature
ontologies.definition: The measure of the level of heat of a human or animal.

ontologies.label: axillary temperature
ontologies.definition: Core body temperature measured in axillary region.

ontologies.label: core body temperature
ontologies.definition: A measurement of the temperature within the deep tissues of the body.

ontologies.label: oral temperature
ontologies.definition: core body temperature measured in sublingual space

ontologies.label: rectal temperature
ontologies.definition: Core body temperature measured in rectum.

ontologies.label: tympanic temperature
ontologies.definition: Core body temperature measured at tympanic membrane.

ontologies.label: blood lipid
ontologies.definition: level and type of lipid found in the blood.

ontologies.label: pulse rate
ontologies.definition: The rate of the pulse as observed in an artery, expressed as beats per minute. It can be measured at several anatomic sites, including the wrist, neck, temple, groin, behind the knees, or on top of the foot.

ontologies.label: peak heart rate during exercise testing
ontologies.definition: The maxium number of times heart beats per minute during exercise test.

ontologies.label: heart rate
ontologies.definition: A measurement that describes the frequency of rate of contractions of the systemic (often left) ventricle measured within a unit time.

ontologies.label: total cholesterol
ontologies.definition: Total cholesterol is defined as the sum of HDL, LDL, and VLDL. Usually, only the total, HDL, and triglycerides are measured.

ontologies.label: triglyceride
ontologies.definition: Fats composed of three fatty acid chains linked to a glycerol molecule.

ontologies.label: high density liptein cholesterol
ontologies.definition: Cholesterol which is contained in or bound to high-density lipoproteins (HDL), including CHOLESTEROL ESTERS and free cholesterol.

ontologies.label: low density lipoprotein cholesterol
ontologies.definition: Cholesterol which is contained in or bound to low density lipoproteins (LDL), including cholesterol esters and free cholesterol.

ontologies.label: muscle strength
ontologies.definition: The amount of force generated by MUSCLE CONTRACTION. Muscle strength can be measured during isometric, isotonic, or isokinetic contraction, either manually or using a device such as a MUSCLE STRENGTH DYNAMOMETER.

ontologies.label: muscle endurance
ontologies.definition: Muscular endurance refers to how long muscles can sustain exercise.

ontologies.label: exergaming
ontologies.definition: video games that are also a form of exercise

ontologies.label: home exercise
ontologies.definition: exercise at home

ontologies.label: athletic injury
ontologies.definition: Injuries incurred during participation in competitive or non-competitive sports.

ontologies.label: physical therapy exercise
ontologies.definition: A regimen or plan of physical activities designed and prescribed for specific therapeutic goals. Its purpose is to restore normal musculoskeletal function or to reduce pain caused by diseases or injuries.

ontologies.label: electrocardiogram
ontologies.definition: A study that evaluates the effect of a treatment on cardiac electrical activity, as assessed by electrocardiography.

ontologies.label: questionnaire
ontologies.definition: Predetermined sets of questions used to collect data - clinical data, social status, occupational group, etc. The term is often applied to a self-completed survey instrument.

ontologies.label: risk stratification
ontologies.definition: a technique for systematically categorizing patients based on their health status and other factors

ontologies.label: exercise stress test
ontologies.definition: Controlled physical activity which is performed in order to allow assessment of physiological functions, particularly cardiovascular and pulmonary, but also aerobic capacity. Maximal (most intense) exercise is usually required but submaximal exercise is also used.

ontologies.label: bioelectric impedance analysis
ontologies.definition: A method to assess body composition, i.e., the relative percentages of body weight comprised of fat tissue and lean body mass. It is based on the principle that the resistance to an applied electric current is inversely related to the amount of lean body mass within the body. Impedance is greatest in fat tissue, which contains only 10-20% water, while lean body mass, which contains 70-75% water, allows the signal to pass much more easily.

ontologies.label: joint mobility exercise
ontologies.definition: Use of active or passive body movement to maintain or restore joint flexibility

ontologies.label: cardiopulmonary exercise test
ontologies.definition: A clinical tool to evaluate exercise capacity and to assess cardiac function under stress.

ontologies.label: balance exercise
ontologies.definition: Use of specific activities, postures, and movements to maintain, enhance, or restore balance

ontologies.label: selective functional movement assessment
ontologies.definition: The SFMA is a clinical model used to assist diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal disorders by identifying dysfunctions in movement patterns.

ontologies.label: Y-balance test
ontologies.definition: a simple, yet reliable, test used to measure dynamic balance

ontologies.label: physical fitness
ontologies.definition: The ability to carry out daily tasks and perform physical activities in a highly functional state, often as a result of physical conditioning.

ontologies.label: cardiorespiratory fitness
ontologies.definition: The ability of the heart and lungs to deliver blood and oxygen to the tissues during aerobic activity. It is a general measure of the relative conditioning of the heart and respiratory system.

ontologies.label: rating of perceived exertion
ontologies.definition: A scale for a subject to rate their perception of the intensity of their own physical effort." [] {comment="NCI: C122028"}

ontologies.label: tummy time
ontologies.definition: Tummy time is a colloquialism for placing infant children in the prone position while awake and supervised, to encourage development of the neck and trunk muscles and prevent skull deformations.

ontologies.label: maximal aerobic power
ontologies.definition: the maximum rate at which oxygen can be used during a specified period, usually during intense exercise" [https://journals.lww.com/acsm-healthfitness/Fulltext/2011/11000/Maximal_Aerobic_Power__An_Important_Clinical_and.12.aspx#\:~\:text=Maximal%20aerobic%20power%20describes%20the%20functional%20capacity%20of\,to%20remove%20and%20use%20oxygen%20from%20the%20blood.] {comment="Maximal aerobic power describes the functional capacity of the cardiorespiratory system."}

ontologies.label: submaximal endurance
ontologies.definition: submaximal endurance capacity. increased by endurance training. average absolute power output a person can maintain during a fixed period of time on cycle ergometer, OR average speed a person can maintain during a fixed period of time.

ontologies.label: morphplogical fitness
ontologies.definition: A non-performance component of physical fitness related to body composition factors such as body circumferences, body fat content and regional body fat distribution.

ontologies.label: body fat distribution
ontologies.definition: Deposits of ADIPOSE TISSUE throughout the body. The pattern of fat deposits in the body regions is an indicator of health status. Excess ABDOMINAL FAT increases health risks more than excess fat around the hips or thighs, therefore, WAIST-HIP RATIO is often used to determine health risks.

ontologies.label: bone density
ontologies.definition: The amount of mineral per square centimeter of BONE. This is the definition used in clinical practice. Actual bone density would be expressed in grams per milliliter. It is most frequently measured by X-RAY ABSORPTIOMETRY or TOMOGRAPHY, X RAY COMPUTED. Bone density is an important predictor for OSTEOPOROSIS.

ontologies.label: muscular fitness
ontologies.definition: Muscular fitness is a general term that describes the general health, strength, and endurance of one's muscles.

ontologies.label: muscular power
ontologies.definition: Muscular power is mainly determined by muscular strength, maximum movement velocity, and neuromuscular activation.

ontologies.label: explosive strength
ontologies.definition: Explosive strength, a component of speed strength, refers to acceleration or rate of force development, or \"the neuromuscular system's ability to generate high action velocities .\

ontologies.label: isometric strength
ontologies.definition: Isometric strength is defined as the capacity to produce force or torque with a voluntary isometric (muscle[s] maintain[s] a constant length) contraction.

ontologies.label: glucose tolerance
ontologies.definition: physiological ability of the body to properly metabolize glucose.

ontologies.label: lipid metabolism
ontologies.definition: Anabolic and catabolic biochemical changes to lipids within a cell as materials needed for important life processes.

ontologies.label: motor fitness
ontologies.definition: Motor fitness is a term that describes an athlete’s ability to perform effectively during sports or other physical activity.

ontologies.label: balance
ontologies.definition: Balance is an ability to maintain the line of gravity (vertical line from centre of mass) of a body within the base of support with minimal postural sway.

ontologies.label: coordination
ontologies.definition: Motor coordination is the orchestrated movement of multiple body parts as required to accomplish intended actions.

ontologies.label: metabolic equivalent of task
ontologies.definition: A mathematic formula used to estimate individual oxygen consumption, and thus energy expenditure, at rest and for various physical activities.

ontologies.label: sleep
ontologies.definition: A readily reversible suspension of sensorimotor interaction with the environment, usually associated with recumbency and immobility.

ontologies.label: resistance training
ontologies.definition: A type of strength-building exercise program that requires the body muscle to exert a force against some form of resistance, such as weight, stretch bands, water, or immovable objects. Resistance exercise is a combination of static and dynamic contractions involving shortening and lengthening of skeletal muscles.

ontologies.label: stretching exercise
ontologies.definition: A physical exercise in which a specific muscle or tendon is deliberately flexed or stretched in order to improve the muscle's elasticity." [] {comment="NCI: C154225"}

ontologies.label: aerobics
ontologies.definition: Aerobics is a form of physical exercise that combines rhythmic aerobic exercise with stretching and strength training routines with the goal of improving all elements of fitness (flexibility, muscular strength, and cardio-vascular fitness).

ontologies.label: badminton
ontologies.definition: Badminton is a racquet sport played using racquets to hit a shuttlecock across a net.

ontologies.label: basketball game
ontologies.definition: A competitive team sport played on a rectangular court having a raised basket at each end.

ontologies.label: boxing
ontologies.definition: A two-person sport in which the fists are skillfully used to attack and defend.

ontologies.label: mind/body exercise
ontologies.definition: A form of exercise that combines body movement with mental focus and controlled breathing to improve strength, balance, flexibility, and overall health. Examples of mind/body exercises are yoga, tai chi, and qigong.

ontologies.label: yoga
ontologies.definition: Yoga as exercise is a physical activity consisting mainly of postures, often connected by flowing sequences, sometimes accompanied by breathing exercises, and frequently ending with relaxation lying down or meditation.

ontologies.label: tai ji
ontologies.definition: A form of traditional Chinese mind/body exercise and meditation that uses slow sets of body movements and controlled breathing. Tai chi is done to improve balance, flexibility, muscle strength, and overall health.

ontologies.label: qigong
ontologies.definition: A form of traditional Chinese mind/body exercise and meditation that uses slow and precise body movements with controlled breathing and mental focusing to improve balance, flexibility, muscle strength, and overall health.

ontologies.label: bicycling
ontologies.definition: Riding a bicycle for transportation or recreation.

ontologies.label: gate ball
ontologies.definition: Gateball is a mallet team sport inspired by croquet.

ontologies.label: hiking
ontologies.definition: Hiking is a long, vigorous walk, usually on trails or footpaths in the countryside.

ontologies.label: jogging
ontologies.definition: Running at a low rate of speed. It can be done as a means of conditioning or for general health and well being.

ontologies.label: swimming
ontologies.definition: The act of propelling the body through water by movement of the arms and/or legs.

ontologies.label: walking
ontologies.definition: The act of traveling by foot.

ontologies.label: brisk walking
ontologies.definition: Brisk walking is a type of exercise where a person walks quickly in order to increase the heart rate and get in shape.

ontologies.label: dancing
ontologies.definition: A physical activity that consists of moving your feet and body rhythmically, usually in response to music.

ontologies.label: fencing
ontologies.definition: Fencing is a group of three related combat sports. The three disciplines in modern fencing are the foil, the épée, and the sabre (also saber); winning points are made through the weapon's contact with an opponent.

ontologies.label: golf
ontologies.definition: A game whose object is to sink a ball into each of 9 or 18 successive holes on a golf course using as few strokes as possible.

ontologies.label: netball game
ontologies.definition: Netball is a ball sport played by two teams of seven players.

ontologies.label: table tennis
ontologies.definition: Table tennis, also known as ping-pong and whiff-whaff, is a sport in which two or four players hit a lightweight ball, also known as the ping-pong ball, back and forth across a table using small rackets.

ontologies.label: skiing
ontologies.definition: A snow sport which uses skis to glide over the snow." [MSH: D012865] {comment="It does not include water-skiing."}

ontologies.label: alpine skiing
ontologies.definition: Alpine skiing, or downhill skiing, is the pastime of sliding down snow-covered slopes on skis with fixed-heel bindings, unlike other types of skiing (cross-country, Telemark, or ski jumping), which use skis with free-heel bindings.

ontologies.label: cross-country skiing
ontologies.definition: Cross-country skiing is a form of skiing where skiers rely on their own locomotion to move across snow-covered terrain, rather than using ski lifts or other forms of assistance.

ontologies.label: taekwondo
ontologies.definition: Taekwondo is a Korean form of martial arts, characterized by punching and kicking techniques, with emphasis on head-height kicks, jumping spinning kicks, and fast kicking techniques.

ontologies.label: tennis
ontologies.definition: A game played by two or four players with rackets and an elastic ball on a level court divided by a low net.

ontologies.label: softball game
ontologies.definition: Softball is a game similar to baseball played with a larger ball (11 to 16 inches or 28 to 40 cm circumference) on a field that has base lengths of 60 feet, a pitcher's mound that ranges from 35 to 43 (professional is 43) feet away from home plate, and a home run fence that is 220–300 feet away from home plate, depending on the type of softball being played.

ontologies.label: association football game
ontologies.definition: A game in which a round inflated ball is advanced by kicking or propelling with any part of the body except the hands or arms. The object of the game is to place the ball in opposite goals.

ontologies.label: squash
ontologies.definition: Squash is a racket and ball sport played by two players in a four-walled court with a small, hollow rubber ball.

ontologies.label: gardening
ontologies.definition: Cultivation of PLANTS; (FRUIT; VEGETABLES; MEDICINAL HERBS) on small plots of ground or in containers.

ontologies.label: yard work
ontologies.definition: The act of tending a yard as a chore or hobby.

ontologies.label: stair climbing
ontologies.definition: Stair climbing is the climbing of a flight of stairs.

ontologies.label: volleyball game
ontologies.definition: A team sport in which two teams hit an inflated ball back and forth over a high net using their hands.

ontologies.label: sprinting
ontologies.definition: Sprinting is running over a short distance at the top-most speed of the body in a limited period of time.

ontologies.label: bodybuilding
ontologies.definition: Bodybuilding is the use of progressive resistance exercise to control and develop one's muscles (muscle building) by muscle hypertrophy for aesthetic purposes.

ontologies.label: strength training
ontologies.definition: resistance exercise that builds strength

ontologies.label: bodyweight exercise
ontologies.definition: Bodyweight exercises (also called bodyweight workouts) are strength-training exercises that use an individual's own weight to provide resistance against gravity.

ontologies.label: suspension training
ontologies.definition: The term suspension training refers to an approach to strength training that uses a system of ropes and webbing called a \"suspension trainer\" to allow users to work against their own body weight.

ontologies.label: weight training
ontologies.definition: Weight training is a common type of strength training for developing the strength and size of skeletal muscles.[2] It uses the force of gravity in the form of weighted bars, dumbbells or weight stacks in order to oppose the force generated by muscle through concentric or eccentric contraction. Weight training uses a variety of specialized equipment to target specific muscle groups and types of movement.

ontologies.label: calisthenics
ontologies.definition: A system of free movements designed to develop muscular tone and promote physical fitness.

ontologies.label: circuit training
ontologies.definition: Circuit training is a form of body conditioning that involves endurance training, resistance training, high-intensity aerobics, and exercises performed in a circuit, similar to high-intensity interval training.

ontologies.label: cross-training
ontologies.definition: Cross-training is athletic training in sports other than the athlete's usual sport. The goal is improving overall performance. It takes advantage of the particular effectiveness of one training method to negate the shortcomings of another.

ontologies.label: birth weight
ontologies.definition: The mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual at BIRTH. It is expressed by units of pounds or kilograms.

ontologies.label: person
ontologies.definition: A living subject of the species homo sapiens.

ontologies.label: interval training
ontologies.definition: Interval training is a type of training exercise that involves a series of high-intensity workouts interspersed with rest or relief periods.

ontologies.label: muscle hypertrophy
ontologies.definition: The muscle system process that results in enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of a muscle organ due to an increase in the size of its muscle cells. Physiological hypertrophy is a normal process during development (it stops in cardiac muscle after adolescence) and can also be brought on in response to demand. In athletes cardiac and skeletal muscles undergo hypertrophy stimulated by increasing muscle activity on exercise. Smooth muscle cells in the uterus undergo hypertrophy during pregnancy.

ontologies.label: pregnant woman
ontologies.definition: Human females who are pregnant, as cultural, psychological, or sociological entities.

ontologies.label: physical therapy
ontologies.definition: The use of exercises and physical activity to restore movement, reduce pain, strengthen muscles, and improve balance and posture in order to restore the ability to function. Therapists provide education and suggest activity modification suited to an individual.

ontologies.label: barbell
ontologies.definition: A barbell is a piece of exercise equipment used in weight training, bodybuilding, weightlifting and powerlifting, consisting of a long bar, usually with weights attached at each end.

ontologies.label: bench
ontologies.definition: Weight training benches may be of various designs: fixed horizontal, fixed inclined, fixed in a folded position, with one adjustable portion, with two or more adjustable portions, with racks to hold bars, etc. In the limit, the definition of a bench blurs into that of combinations that mix a bench and associated equipment. Benches are manufactured by many different vendors, in an array of qualities, features, and prices.

ontologies.label: BOSU
ontologies.definition: A BOSU Balance Trainer (or BOSU ball) is a fitness training device, invented in 1999 by David Weck.[1] It consists of an inflated rubber hemisphere attached to a rigid platform. The device is often used for balance training.

ontologies.label: dumbbell
ontologies.definition: The dumbbell, a type of free weight, is a piece of equipment used in weight training. It can be used individually or in pairs, with one in each hand.

ontologies.label: heavy ropes
ontologies.definition: Battling ropes are used for fitness training to increase full body strength and conditioning.

ontologies.label: kettlebell
ontologies.definition: The kettlebell is a cast iron or cast steel ball with a handle attached to the top (resembling a cannonball with a handle). It is used to perform many types of exercises, including ballistic exercises that combine cardiovascular, strength and flexibility training. They are also the primary equipment used in the weight lifting sport of kettlebell lifting.

ontologies.label: ladder
ontologies.definition: Portable structures typically consisting of two pairs of legs and a series of evenly spaced perpendicular rungs or steps used for climbing. Ladders are typically around 6-10 feet tall, although some shorter ladders (often called stepladders) are approximately 3-4 feet tall and some (called telescoping or extension ladders) may reach up to 20 feet in length. Ladders are typically made of fiberglass, aluminum, or wood.

ontologies.label: medicine ball
ontologies.definition: A medicine ball (also known as an exercise ball, a med ball, or a fitness ball) is a weighted ball whose diameter is about a shoulder-width, (approx. 13.7 inches (350 mm)), often used for rehabilitation and strength training.

ontologies.label: resistance band
ontologies.definition: A resistance band is an elastic band used for strength training. They are also commonly used in physical therapy, specifically by convalescents of muscular injuries, including cardiac rehab patients to allow slow rebuilding of strength.

ontologies.label: stability ball
ontologies.definition: An exercise ball is a ball constructed of soft elastic, typically in 5 diameters of 10-centimeter increments, from 35 centimeters (14 inches) to 85 centimeters (34 inches), and filled with air. The air pressure is changed by removing a valve stem and either filling with air or letting the ball deflate. It is most often used in physical therapy, athletic training and exercise. It can also be used for weight training.

ontologies.label: TRX suspension trainer
ontologies.definition: a performance training tool that leverages gravity and the user’s body weight to complete the exercises

ontologies.label: weight machine
ontologies.definition: A weight machine is an exercise machine used for weight training that uses gravity as the primary source of resistance and a combination of simple machines to convey that resistance to the person using the machine. Each of the simple machines (pulley, lever, wheel, incline) changes the mechanical advantage of the overall machine relative to the weight.

ontologies.label: racket
ontologies.definition: A racket or racquet is a sports implement consisting of a handled frame with an open hoop across which a network of strings or catgut is stretched tightly.

ontologies.label: muscle
ontologies.definition: A fibrous soft tissue with the ability to contract to produce force and motion.

ontologies.label: ball
ontologies.definition: A ball is a round object (usually spherical, but can sometimes be ovoid) with various uses. It is used in ball games, where the play of the game follows the state of the ball as it is hit, kicked or thrown by players. Balls can also be used for simpler activities, such as catch or juggling. Balls made from hard-wearing materials are used in engineering applications to provide very low friction bearings, known as ball bearings. Black-powder weapons use stone and metal balls as projectiles.

ontologies.label: shuttlecock
ontologies.definition: A shuttlecock (also called a birdie or shuttle) is a high-drag projectile used in the sport of badminton. It has an open conical shape formed by feathers or plastic (or a synthetic alternative) embedded into a rounded cork (or rubber) base. The shuttlecock's shape makes it extremely aerodynamically stable. Regardless of initial orientation, it will turn to fly cork first, and remain in the cork-first orientation.

ontologies.label: basketball
ontologies.definition: A basketball is a spherical ball used in basketball games.

ontologies.label: bicycle
ontologies.definition: A bicycle, also called a bike or cycle, is a human-powered or motor-powered, pedal-driven, single-track vehicle, having two wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other.

ontologies.label: golf ball
ontologies.definition: A golf ball is a special ball designed to be used in the game of golf.

ontologies.label: golf club
ontologies.definition: A golf club is a club used to hit a golf ball in a game of golf.

ontologies.label: rope
ontologies.definition: A rope is a group of yarns, plies, fibers or strands that are twisted or braided together into a larger and stronger form.

ontologies.label: ball game
ontologies.definition: Ball games (or ballgames), also ball sports, are any form of game or sport which feature a ball as part of play.

ontologies.label: ski
ontologies.definition: A ski is a narrow strip of semi-rigid material worn underfoot to glide over snow.

ontologies.label: ski pole
ontologies.definition: Ski poles, also referred to as poles (in North America), sticks (UK), or stocks (Australia),[1][2] are used by skiers for balance and propulsion.

ontologies.label: baduanjin
ontologies.definition: The Baduanjin qigong(八段錦) is one of the most common forms of Chinese qigong used as exercise.

ontologies.label: football game
ontologies.definition: Football is a family of team sports that involve, to varying degrees, kicking a ball to score a goal.

ontologies.label: association football
ontologies.definition: A football, soccer ball, football ball, or association football ball is the ball used in the sport of association football.

ontologies.label: rugby football
ontologies.definition: Rugby football is a collective name for the family of team sports of rugby union and rugby league, as well as the earlier forms of football from which both games, as well as Australian rules football and gridiron football, evolved.

ontologies.label: gridiron football game
ontologies.definition: Gridiron football, also known as North American football or, in North America, simply football, is a family of football team sports primarily played in the United States and Canada.

ontologies.label: gridiron football
ontologies.definition: In Canada and the United States, a football (also called a pigskin) is a ball, roughly in the form of a prolate spheroid, used in the context of playing gridiron football.

ontologies.label: American football
ontologies.definition: American football, referred to simply as football in the United States and also known as gridiron, is a team sport played by two teams of eleven players on a rectangular field with goalposts at each end.

ontologies.label: Canadian football
ontologies.definition: Canadian football is a sport played in Canada in which two teams of 12 players each compete for territorial control of a field of play 110 yards (101 m) long and 65 yards (59 m) wide attempting to advance a pointed oval-shaped ball into the opposing team's scoring area (end zone).

ontologies.label: baseball game
ontologies.definition: Baseball is a bat-and-ball game played between two opposing teams, typically of nine players each, that take turns batting and fielding.

ontologies.label: baseball
ontologies.definition: A baseball is a ball used in the sport of the same name. The ball comprises a rubber or cork center wrapped in yarn and covered with white natural horsehide or cowhide, or a synthetic composite leather.

ontologies.label: bat
ontologies.definition: The stick-like implement used to hit the ball in bat-and-ball sports.

ontologies.label: softball bat
ontologies.definition: The bat used by the batter can be made of wood, aluminum, or composite materials such as carbon fiber. Sizes may vary but they may be no more than 34 inches (86 cm) long, 2.4 inches (6 cm) in diameter, or 38 ounces (1.1 kg) in mass." [] {def="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softball#Bat"}

ontologies.label: baseball bat
ontologies.definition: A baseball bat is a smooth wooden or metal club used in the sport of baseball to hit the ball after it is thrown by the pitcher.

ontologies.label: glove
ontologies.definition: A glove is a garment covering the hand." [] {def="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glove"}

ontologies.label: baseball glove
ontologies.definition: A baseball glove or mitt is a large glove (traditionally made of leather, today other options do exist) worn by baseball players of the defending team, which assists players in catching and fielding balls hit by a batter or thrown by a teammate.

ontologies.label: batting glove
ontologies.definition: Batting gloves are a component in bat-and-ball games sportswear. Typically consisting of a leather palm and back made of nylon or another synthetic fabric, the glove covers one or both hands of a batter, providing comfort, prevention of blisters, warmth, improved grip, and shock absorption when hitting the ball. Batting gloves are considered an essential part of cricket equipment, though they are not mandatory at any level of the game.

ontologies.label: bat-and-ball game
ontologies.definition: Bat-and-ball games (or safe haven games) are field games played by two opposing teams, in which the action starts when the defending team throws a ball at a dedicated player of the attacking team, who tries to hit it with a bat and run between various safe areas in the field to score runs (points), while the defending team can use the ball in various ways against the attacking team's players to force them off the field when they are not in safe zones, and thus prevent them from further scoring.

ontologies.label: squash racket
ontologies.definition: Squash rackets have maximum dimensions of 686 mm (27.0 in) long and 215 mm (8.5 in) wide, with a maximum strung area of 500 square centimeters (77.5 sq in). The permitted maximum weight is 255 grams (9.0 oz), but most have a weight between 90 and 150 grams (3–5.3 oz.). The strings of the racket usually have a tension of 25-30.

ontologies.label: squash ball
ontologies.definition: Squash balls are between 39.5 and 40.5 mm in diameter, and weigh 23 to 25 grams. They are made with two pieces of rubber compound, glued together to form a hollow sphere and buffed to a matte finish.

ontologies.label: stair
ontologies.definition: Stairs is a structure designed to bridge a large vertical distance by dividing it into smaller vertical distances, called steps. Stairs may be straight, round, or may consist of two or more straight pieces connected at angles.

ontologies.label: table tennis ball
ontologies.definition: The international rules specify that the game is played with a sphere having a mass of 2.7 grams (0.095 oz) and a diameter of 40 millimetres (1.57 in).

ontologies.label: tennis ball
ontologies.definition: A tennis ball is a ball designed for the sport of tennis. Tennis balls are fluorescent yellow in organised competitions, but in recreational play can be virtually any color. Tennis balls are covered in a fibrous felt which modifies their aerodynamic properties, and each has a white curvilinear oval covering it." [] {def="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_ball"}

ontologies.label: volleyball
ontologies.definition: A volleyball is a ball used to play indoor volleyball, beach volleyball, or other less common variations of the sport. Volleyballs are round and traditionally consist of eighteen nearly rectangular panels of synthetic or genuine leather, arranged in six identical sections of three panels each, wrapped around a bladder. A valve permits the internal air pressure to be adjusted.

ontologies.label: athlete
ontologies.definition: Individuals who have developed skills, physical stamina and strength or participants in SPORTS or other physical activities.

ontologies.label: child
ontologies.definition: An age group comprised of individuals who are not yet an adult. The specific cut-off age will vary by purpose.

ontologies.label: adult
ontologies.definition: An age group comprised of humans who have reached reproductive age.

ontologies.label: elderly
ontologies.definition: An age group comprised of individuals 65 years of age and older.

ontologies.label: postpartum woman
ontologies.definition: commonly used to refer to the females during first six weeks following childbirth

ontologies.label: sensor
ontologies.definition: A device designed to respond to a stimulus by generating a signal that can be measured or interpreted.

ontologies.label: sphygmomanometer
ontologies.definition: Instruments for measuring arterial blood pressure consisting of an inflatable cuff, inflating bulb, and a gauge showing the blood pressure.

ontologies.label: accelerometer
ontologies.definition: An instrument used for measuring a change in velocity.

ontologies.label: wearable electronic device
ontologies.definition: Electronic implements worn on the body as an implant or as an accessory.

ontologies.label: smart glasses
ontologies.definition: Computerized eyewear with multiple technological applications for advanced computing and interoperability. Smart glasses are optimized to facilitate information and data access, capture, display, transfer, and manipulation.

ontologies.label: smart watch
ontologies.definition: A smartwatch is a wearable computer in the form of a watch; modern smartwatches provide a local touchscreen interface for daily use, while an associated smartphone app provides for management and telemetry.

ontologies.label: treadmill
ontologies.definition: A treadmill is a device generally used for walking, running, or climbing while staying in the same place.

ontologies.label: stationary bike
ontologies.definition: A stationary bicycle is a device used as exercise equipment for indoor cycling.

ontologies.label: cardiac rehabilitation
ontologies.definition: Restoration of functions to the maximum degree possible in a person or persons suffering from a CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. It also includes cardiac conditioning and SECONDARY PREVENTION in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk profile.

ontologies.label: fasting plasma glucose
ontologies.definition: Fasting plasma glucose (FPG) levels are determined by taking a blood sample from participants who have fasted for at least 8 hours. It can be measured in mmol/L or in mg/dL. For comparability, these values are converted in mmol/L. Other related biomarkers, such as haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), can be used to help calculate national estimates.

ontologies.label: exercise addiction
ontologies.definition: Exercise addiction is a state characterized by a compulsive engagement in any form of physical exercise, despite negative consequences.

ontologies.label: overweight
ontologies.definition: A status with BODY WEIGHT that is above certain standards. In the scale of BODY MASS INDEX, overweight is defined as having a BMI of 25.0-29.9 kg/m2. Overweight may or may not be due to increases in body fat (ADIPOSE TISSUE), hence overweight does not equal \"over fat\".

ontologies.label: disability
ontologies.definition: Any physical or mental impairment that interferes with an individual's ability to perform desired activities.

ontologies.label: disease
ontologies.definition: A disposition (i) to undergo pathological processes that (ii) exists in an organism because of one or more disorders in that organism.

ontologies.label: aquatic exercise
ontologies.definition: exercise performed in water

ontologies.label: aquatic exercise therapy
ontologies.definition: Aquatic therapy refers to treatments and exercises performed in water for relaxation, fitness, physical rehabilitation, and other therapeutic benefit.

ontologies.label: injury
ontologies.definition: Injury, also known as physical trauma, is damage to the body caused by an external force.

ontologies.label: ligament
ontologies.definition: Shiny, flexible bands of fibrous tissue connecting together articular extremities of bones. They are pliant, tough, and inextensile.

ontologies.label: perimenopausal woman
ontologies.definition: The term \"perimenopausal woman\", which literally means \"woman around the menopause\", refers to woman during the menopause transition years before the date of the final episode of flow.

ontologies.label: spinal cord injury
ontologies.definition: Traumatic damage of the spinal cord.

ontologies.label: cognitive function
ontologies.definition: Cognitive functioning refers to multiple mental abilities, including learning, thinking, reasoning, remembering, problem solving, decision making, and attention.

ontologies.label: physical function
ontologies.definition: An individual's capacity to undertake physical activities, such as everyday tasks.

ontologies.label: waist circumference
ontologies.definition: A circumferential measurement of the waist, which may be classified as the area immediately below the lowest rib, at the narrowest part of the torso, midpoint between the lowest rib and the iliac crest, or immediately above the iliac crest.

ontologies.label: grip strength
ontologies.definition: An assessment of muscle strength that measures that force with which one holds or grasps.

ontologies.label: total daily energy expenditure
ontologies.definition: the Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) + the Thermic Effect of Activity (TEA) + the Thermic Effect of Food (TEF)

ontologies.label: thermic effect of physical activity
ontologies.definition: The thermic effect of physical activity (TEPA) is the amount of energy burned during all physical activity." [https://wikipedikia.org/what-is-the-thermic-effect-of-exercise/] {comment="TEPA can range anywhere from 15 to 30% of TDEE."}

ontologies.label: thermic effect of food
ontologies.definition: Specific dynamic action (SDA), also known as thermic effect of food (TEF) or dietary induced thermogenesis (DIT), is the amount of energy expenditure above the basal metabolic rate due to the cost of processing food for use and storage.

ontologies.label: physical disability
ontologies.definition: A physical disability is a limitation on a person's physical functioning, mobility, dexterity or stamina.

ontologies.label: cool-down exercise
ontologies.definition: Tapering-off physical activity from vigorous to light, to gradually return the body to pre-exercise condition and metabolic state.

ontologies.label: warm-up exercise
ontologies.definition: Physical activities done to prepare the body for more intense physical activities.

ontologies.label: injury of musculoskeletal system
ontologies.definition: Damage to the muscles, bones and their supportive structural attachments.

ontologies.label: bone strength
ontologies.definition: Bone strength can be defined as bone’s resistance to fracture (i.e., failure load) for a given condition (e.g., impact arising from a fall).

ontologies.label: recreational activity
ontologies.definition: Any activity that is intended for refreshment or diversion.

ontologies.label: high-intensity functional training
ontologies.definition: High-intensity functional training (HIFT) is an exercise modality that emphasizes functional, multi-joint movements that can be modified to any fitness level and elicit greater muscle recruitment than more traditional exercise.

ontologies.label: cardiopulmonary endurance
ontologies.definition: Cardiopulmonary endurance is the ability of body to perform aerobic exercise or activity for long periods of time without tiring.

ontologies.label: liuzijue
ontologies.definition: The Six Healing Sounds or Liu Zi Jue is one of the common forms of Chinese qigong, and involves the coordination of movement and breathing patterns with specific sounds.

ontologies.label: range of motion
ontologies.definition: Range of motion (or ROM), is the linear or angular distance that a moving object may normally travel while properly attached to another.

ontologies.label: range of motion exercise
ontologies.definition: Actions performed to provide the active or passive exercises to maintain joint function

ontologies.label: skeletal bone
ontologies.definition: Calcified connective tissue that forms the skeletal components of the body.

ontologies.label: carpal tunnel syndrome
ontologies.definition: Entrapment of the MEDIAN NERVE in the carpal tunnel, which is formed by the flexor retinaculum and the CARPAL BONES.

ontologies.label: rotator cuff injury
ontologies.definition: Injuries to the ROTATOR CUFF of the shoulder joint.

ontologies.label: tennis elbow
ontologies.definition: A condition characterized by pain in or near the lateral humeral epicondyle or in the forearm extensor muscle mass as a result of unusual strain. It occurs due repetitive stresses on the elbow from activities such as tennis playing.

ontologies.label: injury of cruciate ligament of knee
acceleration
ontologies.definition: An increase in the rate of speed.

ontologies.label: electromyography
ontologies.definition: Recording of the changes in electric potential of muscle by means of surface or needle electrodes.

ontologies.label: galvanic skin response
ontologies.definition: A change in electrical resistance of the skin, occurring in emotion and in certain other conditions.

ontologies.label: oxygen saturation
ontologies.definition: Extent to which HEMOGLOBIN is saturated with OXYGEN typically as measured in arterial blood. It can be measured by various methods (e.g., PULSE OXYMETER, blood gas analysis). A low blood oxygen saturation level indicates a condition called HYPOXEMIA.

ontologies.label: molecule
ontologies.definition: An aggregate of two or more atoms in a defined arrangement held together by chemical bonds.

ontologies.label: dopamine
ontologies.definition: One of the catecholamine NEUROTRANSMITTERS in the brain. It is derived from TYROSINE and is the precursor to NOREPINEPHRINE and EPINEPHRINE. Dopamine is a major transmitter in the extrapyramidal system of the brain, and important in regulating movement. A family of receptors (RECEPTORS, DOPAMINE) mediate its action.

ontologies.label: endorphin
ontologies.definition: One of the three major groups of endogenous opioid peptides. They are large peptides derived from the PRO-OPIOMELANOCORTIN precursor. The known members of this group are alpha-, beta-, and gamma-endorphin. The term endorphin is also sometimes used to refer to all opioid peptides, but the narrower sense is used here; OPIOID PEPTIDES is used for the broader group.

ontologies.label: serotonin
ontologies.definition: A biochemical messenger and regulator, synthesized from the essential amino acid L-TRYPTOPHAN. In humans it is found primarily in the central nervous system, gastrointestinal tract, and blood platelets. Serotonin mediates several important physiological functions including neurotransmission, gastrointestinal motility, hemostasis, and cardiovascular integrity. Multiple receptor families (RECEPTORS, SEROTONIN) explain the broad physiological actions and distribution of this biochemical mediator.

ontologies.label: norepinephrine
ontologies.definition: Precursor of epinephrine that is secreted by the ADRENAL MEDULLA and is a widespread central and autonomic neurotransmitter. Norepinephrine is the principal transmitter of most postganglionic sympathetic fibers, and of the diffuse projection system in the brain that arises from the LOCUS CERULEUS. It is also found in plants and is used pharmacologically as a sympathomimetic.

ontologies.label: neurotransmitter
ontologies.definition: Endogenous signaling molecules secreted by neurons that alter the behavior of neurons or effector cells. Neurotransmitter is used here in its most general sense, including not only messengers that act directly to regulate ion channels, but also those that act through second messenger systems, and those that act at a distance from their site of release. Included are neuromodulators, neuroregulators, neuromediators, neurohormones, and neurohumors, whether or not acting at synapses.

ontologies.label: adenosine triphosphate
ontologies.definition: An adenine nucleotide containing three phosphate groups esterified to the sugar moiety. In addition to its crucial roles in metabolism adenosine triphosphate is a neurotransmitter.

ontologies.label: glutamate
ontologies.definition: A non-essential alpha-amino acid and excitatory neurotransmitter. Glutamic acid can serve as a precursor for the synthesis of the inhibitory neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA).

ontologies.label: rehabilitation therapy
ontologies.definition: A therapeutic procedure whose objective is to improve functioning of parts of the body involved in macro movements and whose current level of functioning are clinically abnormal.

ontologies.label: physical therapy
ontologies.definition: A rehabilitation therapy that improves functioning by (1) increasing muscle strength, range of motion, flexibility, or balance, or (2) reducing pain, either one through non-invasive manipulations of the body.

ontologies.label: occupational therapy
ontologies.definition: A rehabilitation therapy whose objective is to improve functioning in activities of daily living or occupational tasks, often using supportive devices in contact with the body as aids or through alterations in the patient’s home or work environment.

ontologies.label: rehabilitation therapy cue
ontologies.definition: A communication that is part of a rehabilitation therapy, whose active participant is the bearer of a therapist role and the GDC communicated is one or more objective specifications or action specifications.

ontologies.label: guided rehabilitation therapy cue
ontologies.definition: A rehabilitation therapy cue that communicates an objective specification and invites, either implicitly or explicitly, the patient to find an action specification that achieves the objective.

ontologies.label: directed rehabilitation therapy cue
ontologies.definition: A rehabilitation therapy cue that communicates an action specification to achieve an objective of the therapy.

ontologies.label: rehabilitation encounter
ontologies.definition: A health care encounter that realizes the physiatrist role of a participant and has a rehabilitation therapy as a part.

ontologies.label: physical therapy encounter
ontologies.definition: A health care encounter that realizes the physical therapist role of a participant and has the provision of physical therapy as a part.

ontologies.label: occupational therapy encounter
ontologies.definition: A health care encounter that realizes the occupational therapist role of a participant and has the provision of occupational therapy as a part.

ontologies.label: occupational therapist role
ontologies.definition: An institutional health care role that is created by training and certification in occupational therapy and that is realized by the provision of occupational therapy.

ontologies.label: meta-cognitive strategy training
ontologies.definition: A therapeutic procedure that actively engages patients in identifying the key bodily-functional limitations they wish to work on, self-assessing those limitations, developing objective specifications for addressing those limitations, developing new action specifications to achieve those objectives, and then implementing those actions towards those objectives.

ontologies.label: active assisted range of motion process
ontologies.definition: A range of motion exercise that is carried out by the organism and assisted by a force in addition to the contraction of the muscles that move the joint.

ontologies.label: joint motion
ontologies.definition: A bodily process whereby the bones articulated by a joint change relative positions and orientations with respect to one another.

ontologies.label: musculoskeletal system function
altLabels: function of a part of the musculoskeletal system
ontologies.definition: A function that inheres in some part of the musculoskeletal system.

ontologies.label: nervous system function
altLabels: function of a part of the nervous system
ontologies.definition: A function that inheres in some part of the nervous system.

ontologies.label: bodily movement function
ontologies.definition: A musculoskeletal system function that is realized by intentional muscle contractions that set one or more body parts in motion.

ontologies.label: motor control function
altLabels: motor control function of the nervous system
ontologies.definition: A function that inheres in the nervous system of an organism and that is realized by coordination of goal-directed movements through integrated nervous system activity.

ontologies.label: bodily mobility function
ontologies.definition: A function that inheres in an organism and that is complex, being comprised of a bodily movement function and a motor control function, and that is realized by locomotion.

ontologies.label: wheeled walker
ontologies.definition: A locomotion assistive device that (1) supports the body in an upright standing position, (2) has a frame with four legs as part, (3) has two or more wheels as part, and (4) whose locomotion function, if realized, is realized by a process that (a) has as part rolling of its wheels while the organism walks and (b) has continuous (i.e., uninterrupted) support of the organisms weight.

ontologies.label: hemi walker
ontologies.definition: A locomotion assistive device that (1) supports the body in an upright standing position, (2) has four legs as part, (3) is designed to be operated with a single upper limb, and (4) whose locomotion function, if realized, is realized by a process that has alternating parts of (a) weight support and (b) non-weight support when the device is either slid forward, or lifted in the air to move it forward, before the next weight supporting part.

ontologies.label: single point cane
ontologies.definition: A locomotion assistive device that (1) supports the body in an upright standing position, (2) has a single point of contact with the ground as part, (3) has as part a handle where the organism grasps it during locomotion, and (4) whose locomotion function, if realized, is realized by a process that has alternating parts of (a) weight support and (b) non-weight support when the device is lifted in the air to move it forward before the next weight supporting part.

ontologies.label: quad cane
ontologies.definition: A locomotion assistive device that (1) supports the body in an upright standing position, (2) has four points of contact with the ground as part, (3) has as part a handle where the organism grasps it during locomotion, and (4) whose locomotion function, if realized, is realized by a process that has alternating parts of (a) weight support and (b) non-weight support when the device is lifted in the air to move it forward before the next weight supporting part.

ontologies.label: sliding board
ontologies.definition: A locomotion assistive device that (1) supports the body in a seated position, (2) is a rigid flat surface, and (3) whose locomotion function, if realized, is realized by a process that has as part sliding of the organism from one seated surface to another.

ontologies.label: physical therapist role
ontologies.definition: An institutional health care role that is created by training and certification in physical therapy and that is realized by the provision of physical therapy.

ontologies.label: medical device
ontologies.definition: An object manufactured with a function either (1) to diagnose, cure, mitigate, treat, or prevent disease or (2) to alter physically (i.e., not chemically) the structure or functioning of some part of the body of an organism.

ontologies.label: activity of daily living assistive device
ontologies.definition: A medical device whose function is to improve the degree (or quality) of realization of an organism's capability to perform one or more activities of daily living.

ontologies.label: locomotion assistive device
ontologies.definition: An activity of daily living assistive device whose function is to improve the degree of realization of an organism's capability for locomotion.

ontologies.label: assistive device for donning or removing clothing
ontologies.definition: An activity of daily living assistive device whose function is to improve the degree of realization of an organism's capability to don or remove one or more articles of clothing.

ontologies.label: grasping or holding assistive device
ontologies.definition: An object manufactured with the function to enhance an organism's capability to grasp or hold onto other objects.

ontologies.label: wheelchair
ontologies.definition: A locomotion assistive device that (1) supports the body in a seated position, (2) has two or more wheels as part, and (3) whose locomotion function, if realized, is realized by a process that has as part rotating of its wheels.

ontologies.label: facilitation-requiring disposition
ontologies.definition: A disposition inhering in a material entity that is necessarily facilitated by some other disposition.

ontologies.label: facilitating
ontologies.definition: A process that realizes a realizable entity y and that is a proper occurrent part of a process that realizes a realizable entity x, where x does not equal y and x is facilitated by y.

ontologies.label: requires physical assistance disposition
ontologies.definition: A facilitation-requiring disposition inhering in a part of an organism and that is clinically abnormal.

ontologies.label: requires assistive device disposition
ontologies.definition: A requires physical assistance disposition that is necessarily facilitated by the function of an assistive device.

ontologies.label: requires personal assistance disposition
ontologies.definition: A requires physical assistance disposition that is necessarily facilitated by a disposition inhering in another organism.

ontologies.label: sock aid
ontologies.definition: A dressing assistive device made of plastic that (1) has one or more long straps or cords attached to its body as part, (2) is designed to hold a sock or stocking open when placed inside it, and (3) whose donning function, if realized, is realized by a process that has as part the organism's foot sliding into the sock and the sock being pulled over the heel while the device holds the sock open, without the organism bending at the waist.

ontologies.label: dressing stick
ontologies.definition: A dressing assistive device that (1) is a rigid elongated shaft, and (2) has one or more hooks as part at one or both ends, and (3) whose donning or removing function, if realized, is realized by a process that has as part a hook engaging an article of clothing to pull it onto, or push or pull it off of, part of the organism's body.

ontologies.label: shoe horn
ontologies.definition: A dressing assistive device that (1) has a curved, rigid blade-shaped body, and (2) whose donning function, if realized, is realized by a process that has as part the organism's heel sliding along the device's curved surface into the back of a shoe.

ontologies.label: long handled shoe horn
ontologies.definition: A shoe horn that has an elongated handle as part, sufficient to enable donning a shoe without the organism bending at the waist.

ontologies.label: reacher device
ontologies.definition: A grasping or holding assistive device that (1) is an elongated rigid or semi-rigid shaft, (2) has a jaw or claw mechanism as part at the distal end, (3) has a trigger or lever as part at the proximal (handle) end that operates the jaw, and (4) whose grasping or holding function, if realized, is realized by a process that has as part closing of the jaw around an object at a distance from the organism's body.

ontologies.label: bodily energy expenditure
ontologies.definition: A bodily process that releases energy from bodily energy stores and that is an occurrent part of another bodily process.

ontologies.label: physical exertion
ontologies.definition: A bodily energy expenditure that is an occurrent part of muscle contraction.

ontologies.label: requires minimal personal assistance disposition
ontologies.definition: A requires personal assistance disposition whose realization requires as occurrent part minimal physical exertion on the part of the other organism relative to its bearer.

ontologies.label: requires moderate personal assistance disposition
ontologies.definition: A requires personal assistance disposition whose realization requires as occurrent part roughly the same physical exertion on the part of the other organism relative to its bearer.

ontologies.label: requires maximal personal assistance disposition
ontologies.definition: A requires personal assistance disposition whose realization requires far more physical exertion on the part of the other organism relative to its bearer.

ontologies.label: requires total personal assistance disposition
ontologies.definition: A requires personal assistance disposition whose realization requires that all physical exertion is on the part of the other organism.

ontologies.label: patient lift
ontologies.definition: An activity of daily living assistive device that uses electrical or hydraulic power to elevate a person above a resting surface and then lower them back down to a resting surface.

ontologies.label: range of motion process
ontologies.definition: A joint motion all the way to one extreme of apposition of the bones in the joint that is permitted by any ligaments, tendons, capsules, and muscles that are either part of the joint or connected to same.

ontologies.label: active range of motion process
ontologies.definition: A range of motion process effected solely by the intentional control of the organism through contraction of the muscles that move the joint.

ontologies.label: passive range of motion process
ontologies.definition: A range of motion process carried out by assistance from a force other than the muscles that move the joint and that pushes the joint to a greater extreme than is typically possible by the organism on its own.

ontologies.label: joint function
ontologies.definition: A function inhering in a joint.

ontologies.label: muscle function
ontologies.definition: A function inhering in a muscle.

ontologies.label: range of motion function of a joint
ontologies.definition: A Joint function that is realized by a range of motion process.

ontologies.label: power of a muscle
ontologies.definition: A function of a muscle to generate force per unit time via contraction.

ontologies.label: strength of a muscle
ontologies.definition: A function of a muscle to generate force via contraction.

ontologies.label: physical exercise
ontologies.definition: A bodily process that is intentional, has an objective of increasing the functioning of some part(s) of the body, is repetitive, and has one or more components of the musculoskeletal system as participants.

ontologies.label: range of motion exercise
ontologies.definition: A physical exercise whose objective is to maintain the range of motion function of a joint or improve it towards clinically normal (when not currently normal) and whose repetitions are range of motion processes

ontologies.label: active range of motion exercise
ontologies.definition: A range of motion exercise whose repetitions are active range of motion processes.

ontologies.label: passive range of motion exercise
ontologies.definition: A range of motion exercise whose repetitions are passive range of motion processes.

ontologies.label: active assisted range of motion exercise
ontologies.definition: A range of motion exercise whose repetitions are active assisted range of motion processes.

ontologies.label: strength exercise
ontologies.definition: A physical exercise whose objective is to increase the strength of one or more muscles.

ontologies.label: power exercise
ontologies.definition: A physical exercise whose objective is to increase the power of one or more muscles.

ontologies.label: task object role
ontologies.definition: The role of an object during rehabilitation therapy that is realized by the patient performing activities that realize a function of the object, such that the patient increasingly improves their capability(ies) to use an object of a similar type.
